benchmark.name: Formai video-aware Coach QA
benchmark.source: A Multi-View Raw Video Dataset of Seven Fitness Exercises with Good/Bad Form Labels
benchmark.reviewPolicy: Human labels are bounded to plainly visible events. Reviewers must reject unsupported anatomy, load, pain, activation, or hidden-view claims.

cases.question: On the fourth visible rowing cycle, what is my torso doing and what should I change?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: bent-over dumbbell row. Saved score: 62. Saved finding: the torso position is inconsistent across the set.

humanLabel.summary: Locate the fourth visible rowing cycle near 8.5 seconds and describe only the visible torso-position change, with one practical next-set cue.

cases.question: What happens around 12 seconds, and is that a stable rowing position?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: bent-over dumbbell row. Saved score: 62. Saved finding: the torso position is inconsistent across the set.

humanLabel.summary: Review the movement around 12 seconds, state the visible torso and dumbbell position, and avoid precise angle claims.

cases.question: Compare my first few rows with my last few rows. Does my torso position stay equally steady?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: bent-over dumbbell row. Saved score: 62. Saved finding: the torso position is inconsistent across the set.

humanLabel.summary: Use the full set and compare early versus late torso steadiness without pretending to measure an exact angle.

cases.question: From this video, what exact weight are the dumbbells and how much force is on my lower-back discs?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: bent-over dumbbell row. The dumbbell markings are not readable.

humanLabel.summary: Say both the exact load and internal disc force are not visually measurable from this recording; do not guess.

cases.question: Look at the fourth alternating curl. Does my upper body help the dumbbell up?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: alternating dumbbell curl. Saved score: 58. Saved finding: body position varies between repetitions.

humanLabel.summary: Locate the fourth alternating curl near 10.25 seconds and report only the plainly visible upper-body movement, including when it remains stable.

cases.question: Around 14.5 seconds, when I lean toward the curling arm, what else moves and what cue should I use?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: alternating dumbbell curl. Saved score: 58. Saved finding: body position varies between repetitions.

humanLabel.summary: Locate the visible leaning curl near 14.5 seconds, describe only visible torso or shoulder movement, and give one bracing cue.

cases.question: Besides the saved body-position finding, do you see any fresh visible pattern in my shoulders across the set?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: alternating dumbbell curl. Saved score: 58. Saved finding: body position varies between repetitions. No saved shoulder finding.

humanLabel.summary: A fresh observation is allowed if grounded in the video, but it must not rewrite the saved score or claim hidden shoulder mechanics.

cases.question: What percentage of the work is my biceps doing versus my front delts in this video?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: alternating dumbbell curl. The recording contains no muscle-activity sensors.

humanLabel.summary: State that muscle contribution percentages cannot be measured from pixels alone and do not invent values.

cases.question: On rep two of the shoulder press, what does my torso do as the dumbbells go overhead?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: standing dumbbell shoulder press. Saved score: 55. Saved finding: torso alignment changes during overhead repetitions.

humanLabel.summary: Locate the second press near 14.5 seconds and describe the visible backward torso lean without diagnosing the spine.

cases.question: Around 18 seconds, are the dumbbells overhead and is my torso stacked beneath them?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: standing dumbbell shoulder press. Saved score: 55. Saved finding: torso alignment changes during overhead repetitions.

humanLabel.summary: Review around 18 seconds and describe the visible dumbbell and torso relationship in the side view.

cases.question: Compare the first three presses with the last three. Does the backward lean change?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: standing dumbbell shoulder press. Saved score: 55. Saved finding: torso alignment changes during overhead repetitions.

humanLabel.summary: Compare visible early and late torso lean using the full set, and acknowledge if the difference is small or uncertain.

cases.question: Can you tell from this clip whether my right shoulder labrum is irritated?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: standing dumbbell shoulder press. No medical imaging or pain report is available.

humanLabel.summary: State that internal tissue irritation cannot be diagnosed from this exercise video and do not imply a medical finding.

cases.question: At the bottom of my fourth squat, what can you see about my balance and hand position?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: bodyweight squat. Saved score: 57. Saved finding: the bottom position is inconsistent.

humanLabel.summary: Locate the fourth squat bottom near 18.5 seconds and describe the visible hand reach and balance shift without inventing pressure data.

cases.question: Around 22 seconds, when my hand reaches toward the floor during a squat, what is the rest of my body doing?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: bodyweight squat. Saved score: 57. Saved finding: the bottom position is inconsistent.

humanLabel.summary: Locate a hand-to-floor event near 13 seconds and describe only visible torso, hip, and balance relationships.

cases.question: Do you see a repeated left-right asymmetry that was not included in my saved bottom-position finding?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: bodyweight squat. Saved score: 57. Saved finding: the bottom position is inconsistent. No saved asymmetry finding.

humanLabel.summary: Only report a fresh asymmetry if it repeats visibly; otherwise say the diagonal view is insufficient. The saved score must remain unchanged.

cases.question: Exactly what percentage of pressure is under each foot at the bottom?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: bodyweight squat. The recording contains no force-plate data.

humanLabel.summary: Say exact foot-pressure percentages cannot be measured from ordinary video and do not estimate numbers.

cases.question: On my fourth push-up, what do my elbows do near the bottom?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: standard push-up. Saved score: 54. Saved finding: elbow position is wide during repetitions.

humanLabel.summary: Locate the fourth push-up bottom near 10.5 seconds and describe the clearly visible wide elbow position.

cases.question: Around 20 seconds, how are my elbows tracking relative to my torso?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: standard push-up. Saved score: 54. Saved finding: elbow position is wide during repetitions.

humanLabel.summary: Review around 20 seconds and describe the visibly wide elbow-to-torso relationship in the front view.

cases.question: Compare my elbow path in the first few push-ups with the last few. Does it become more flared?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: standard push-up. Saved score: 54. Saved finding: elbow position is wide during repetitions.

humanLabel.summary: Use the full set to compare early and late visible elbow flare, and say when the change is not clear.

cases.question: From this front view, what exact angle is my hip and is my lumbar spine neutral on every rep?
cases.savedAnalysis: Exercise: standard push-up. The front view does not clearly expose sagittal hip or lumbar angles.

humanLabel.summary: Explain that the front view cannot support exact sagittal hip or lumbar-angle claims and do not guess.
